name: Household messages
description: 66 texts and emails a household gets (bills, family, spam, appointments, deliveries, school), 12 of them deliberately tricky: phishing dressed as a bill, urgent news written casually, negated deadlines.
context: Messages received by a family household (two parents, two kids in elementary school).

criteria.bills: A legitimate charge, payment request, balance, or statement from a company, landlord, utility, or service the household uses
criteria.family: A personal message from a relative or friend, whatever it is about
criteria.spam: Unsolicited marketing, a scam, or phishing, including fake notices that imitate real companies or suspicious links
criteria.appointment: Scheduling, confirming, or reminding about an appointment or service visit (doctor, dentist, vet, repair, haircut, DMV)
criteria.delivery: Package, order, or food delivery status from a retailer or carrier
criteria.school: A message from the kids' school, teacher, district, or PTA

action_today.instructions: Someone in the household needs to do something today because of `item`.

criteria.true: A deadline today or tomorrow, a same-day reply or pickup requested, or something goes wrong if it's ignored today
criteria.false: Informational, a later deadline, no action needed, or spam that should simply be ignored
